programs.title: Pad A Girl Child
programs.description:
Impact in action! 

As part of our Pad A Girl intervention in Langtang North, OCHAWORTHLACDI in partnership with bambam soya oil distributed 350 sanitary pads to girls at Government Secondary School (GSS) Langtang.

Every pad distributed represents more than menstrual hygiene ... it represents dignity, confidence, and a girl’s right to stay in school without interruption.

Together, we are breaking stigma, fighting period poverty, and creating a future where no girl is held back by her period.

Changing lives, one girl at a time !!!❤️

Our Pad A Girl intervention continued at Government Secondary School (GSS) Shishiri, Langtang North, where girls received sanitary pads and menstrual health education.

In collaboration with @bambamsoyaoil , we are helping girls manage their periods with dignity, stay in school, and pursue their dreams without interruption.

Together, we’re breaking stigma, ending period poverty, and creating a future where every girl has the support she needs to thrive.

programs.title: World Cancer Day Walk
programs.description:
OWLACDI and the Plateau Health Ministry are really pushing for cancer awareness and early detection in Plateau State. The message is clear: cancer isn’t a death sentence if caught early and treated properly.

Some key takeaways:
- *United by Unique*: Emphasizing personalized care and collective action against cancer.
- *Awareness and Screening*: Many still lack basic knowledge about cancer; promoting early detection and screenings is crucial.
- *Government Support*: Need for prioritized cancer research, treatment, and affordable care, especially for vulnerable groups.
- *Prevention*: Vaccination, healthy lifestyles, and avoiding risk factors can reduce cancer risk.

The Plateau State Government is strengthening cancer prevention and control through public awareness, screenings, and collaborations. What’s your take on how communities can support cancer awareness?

programs.title: Breast Cancer Awareness
programs.description:
The overarching aim of the project is to advance health equity and reduce breast cancer mortality in Plateau State by establishing sustainable grassroots awareness, facilitating early detection pathways, and providing direct patient navigation support for underserved communities in Jos.
To achieve this, the campaign will execute four core, measurable objectives:

Objective 1 (Community Education): Educate and empower 1,000+ youth, students, and low-income community members across Jos North and Jos South LGAs on proper Breast Self-Examination (BSE) protocols, early warning signs, and proactive risk-reduction behaviors by October 31, 2026.

Objective 2 (Clinical Screening and Referral): Facilitate free, high-quality Clinical Breast Examinations (CBE) and provide structured diagnostic navigation and referral pathways for at least 150 low-income, underserved women in target peri-urban communities in Jos.

Objective 3 (Social Justice and Policy Advocacy): Mobilize regional conversations linking healthcare access to structural social justice, presenting a comprehensive policy brief to health stakeholders in Plateau State regarding the elimination of financial barriers to screening.

Objective 4 (Patient Solidarity and Material Support): Mobilize community-led fundraising and material resource provision to provide direct palliative, psychological, and logistical care items to active breast cancer patients currently undergoing therapy at tertiary oncology wards in Jos.

The campaign specifically channels resources toward high-vulnerability cohorts across Jos and its surrounding demographics:

a.	Market Women and Low-Income Urban Dwellers: Centered primarily in highly populated local trade hubs (e.g., Terminus Market, Katako Market), where out-of-pocket healthcare expenditures are intensely minimized by economic pressures.

b.	Youths and Tertiary Students: Targeting female students across major regional institutions (e.g., University of Jos, Plateau State Polytechnic), utilizing peer-led structures to instill lifelong early-detection behaviors.

c.	Oncology Patients, Survivors, and Caregivers: Engaging directly with individuals navigating active therapeutic regimens within regional tertiary hospitals to foster structural peer support groups and ease financial distress.
